Commentary.Commentary: We are back for New Zealand's replay! Zimbabwe players are in a huddle where Sean Williams is giving them a last-minute pep talk before they take the field. Will Young and Devon Conway are the two openers for New Zealand. Blessing Muzarabani to start proceedings with the ball. Let's go...
... SECOND INNINGS ...

For the visitors, Matt Henry was the standout bowler, displaying pinpoint accuracy and claiming an impressive 6 wickets. Nathan Smith also chipped in with 3 wickets, further exposing Zimbabwe's batting vulnerabilities. With Zimbabwe's innings now over, the focus shifts to New Zealand's batting lineup and how they will capitalize on the hosts' struggles.

Zimbabwe's batting unit struggled to get going, and they were eventually bundled out for a modest 149 runs. The Kiwi bowlers were relentless, not allowing any significant partnerships to form and taking wickets at regular intervals. Although Nick Welch, Craig Ervine, and Tafadzwa Tsiga showed some resistance, it wasn't enough to propel Zimbabwe to a competitive first innings total.

Commentary.Commentary: We are back for the final session on Day 1! New Zealand players are making their way out to the middle with a target to bowl the hosts out as soon as possible. Newman Nyamhuri and Vincent Masekesa will resume the batting for Zimbabwe and hopefully extend the total closer to 200. Mitchell Santner to bowl after Tea. Here we go...
... DAY 1, SESSION 3 ...

How long can the hosts bat? Can they try and scrape through to 175? That will not serve any purpose in terms of a good total on this surface, but at least, it will give them some kind of a psychological belief. Additionally, if they can manage to bat for just a bit over an hour, they can stir some nerves in the Kiwi camp by bowling at their batters with around 30-45 minutes for the close. 35 overs left in the day, so we should not need too much of the extended half hour. The third session should begin somewhere around 1300 GMT.

Difficult period for the home side. Won the toss, chose to bat, but instead of batters surviving through the tough period, they have just kept on losing wickets. Only four batters have reached double digits so far and that reflects on the fact that the batters have tried to bed in, but then the cot has got broken. The on-air commentators are hopeful of Zimbabwe doing the same to the Kiwi batters but we believe that the Kiwis have got a stronger technique in batting and discipline than their opponents.

The Kiwis started the post-Lunch session with a brute to dismiss Sikandar Raza but after that, though they had to struggle to pick up wickets regularly, did manage to get rid of the captain, albeit, with some luck. And then, the wicket of Tsiga meant that they are well and truly into the tail. The wickets' column has been filled only for Matt Henry and Nathan Smith but everyone has bowled well.

Slow moving in Bulawayo. 71/3 in 28.4 overs in that session, with the game going absolutely nowhere for Zimbabwe. The Kiwis will not mind it, as they are probably just 5-6 overs away from wiping this tail off.

Commentary.Commentary: The players are back out in the middle. There was some turn on purchase in the morning session, so we could see even more of that as the sun beats down hard. Sikandar Raza has walked out at number 6, alongside skipper Craig Ervine, after the fall of Welch's wicket, and the duo will aim for a partnership in the first place. Here we go then, Henry to resume.

It was a difficult opening session for the home side. But from what we have seen in the previous matches, especially when South Africa toured the country, the first session has always been kind of a havoc for batters. In the afternoon though, the deck usually settles down and batting is a lot easier. That's why that wicket of Welch would be hurting the hosts the most, because having faced 67 balls prior to his dismissal, he would have done a lot better in the second session.
... DAY 1, SESSION 2 ...

Matt Henry has been the pick of the bowlers, claiming three wickets, while Nathan Smith also chipped in with a scalp. In the second session, Zimbabwe will need to start anew and get their scoreboard ticking if they want to get back into the game. Can Craig Ervine, alongside Sikandar Raza and others, build a substantial partnership and take the hosts out of trouble? The battle resumes after Lunch at 10.38 am GMT.

However, the partnership between Nick Welch and Craig Ervine was showing promise, with both batters playing carefully and rotating the strike. However, just before Lunch, Mitchell Santner's astute bowling change brought Matt Henry back into the attack, which paid off for the Kiwis. Nick Welch edged a delivery straight to Michael Bracewell at slip, falling victim to Henry's skill. The wicket came at a crucial time, right on the stroke of Lunch, with Zimbabwe still in a precarious position at 67/4.

The first session of Day 1 has come to a close, with New Zealand dominating the proceedings. Zimbabwe's batting unit struggled, managing 67 runs in 26.2 overs for the loss of 4 wickets. The top three batters were dismissed with just 31 runs on the board, putting the hosts in a precarious position.

OUT! TAKEN! Matt Henry strikes again! A hammer blow to Zimbabwe on the stroke of Lunch. This is an inspired bowling change from the Kiwi skipper. Henry lands this one back of a length and just around off, holds its line. Nick Welch gets tempted and pushes hard at it, but without much footwork. Gets a thick outside edge towards second slip where Michael Bracewell takes a sharp catch. Welch's resistance is finally broken as he departs for 27 off 68, and Zimbabwe are 67/4. THAT WILL BE LUNCH ON DAY 1!

Commentary.Commentary: The stage is set for an exciting Test match between Zimbabwe and New Zealand! The umpires are in place, and the players are ready to take to the field. Brian Bennett and Ben Curran are walking out to bat for Zimbabwe, while Matt Henry is preparing to bowl the first over of the match for New Zealand. Let's get ready to witness some thrilling cricket!

We are not far away from the action, but before that, the match officials and players from both sides make their way out to the middle and line up for their respective national anthems. It will be New Zealand's first followed by the national anthem of Zimbabwe.

Ben Curran of Zimbabwe also shared a few words. He expressed his excitement about returning to action for Zimbabwe after recovering from a broken knuckle. He revealed that the injury required 3-4 weeks of rest, but the downtime allowed him to focus on his game. Curran spent quality time in the nets, which he believes has been beneficial. He watched the Test series against South Africa and learned from it, acknowledging it was tough to watch. Curran is looking forward to the new pitch and believes the team's preparations have been good. He emphasized the importance of giving their best in the upcoming Test series, seeing it as an opportunity to showcase their skills with both bat and ball. Curran expressed the team's desire to bounce back strong after a tough period.

Rachin Ravindra of New Zealand is up for a quick chat. He says that it was a great tri-series,  but now it is time to adopt to the longer format. Adds that in this format, that win in India was special and they can take inspiration from that. Mentions that it is very tough to replace someone like Kane Williamson, but each and everyone wants to contribute as they can. Says that they have an exciting bowling group with Matt Henry and Will O'Rourke being excellent, Nathan Smith doing well and Matthew Fisher coming into the squad brings depth and variety.

Mitchell Santner, the skipper of New Zealand, says that they would have batted first as well. Adds that it is unfortunate for Latham to miss out, but it also gives opportunity to the team to step up. Mentions that the first hour will be crucial to make inroads. Ends by saying that it is always an honour to lead the side.

Zimbabwe captain Craig Ervine has decided to bat first, citing the wicket's dry conditions as a factor. He emphasized the importance of scoring runs early on to set up a strong foundation and potentially utilize their spinners later in the game. Ervine stressed that the batting group needs to be alert from the start and perform better, highlighting the need for caution in the first 20 balls and a positive body language, which was lacking in their previous series against South Africa. The team has benefited from a break and intense training, and several key players have returned to the side, including Ben Curran, Brian Bennett, and Sikandar Raza. The bowling unit has also seen the inclusion of Vincent Masekesa and Newman Nyamhuri.

PITCH RPORT - Ed Rainsford and Scott Styris shared their insights on the pitch for Day 1 of the Test match in Bulawayo. Rainsford noted that the surface looks similar to the one they experienced against South Africa, with the average score in the first innings batting first being around 400. Styris added that the pitch has a lot of grass cover, which might make it slower, and variable bounce can be expected. He also pointed out a few rough patches that spinners can exploit, making it an interesting contest between batters and bowlers.

New Zealand (Playing XI) - Devon Conway, Will Young, Henry Nicholls, Rachin Ravindra, Daryl Mitchell, Tom Blundell (WK), Michael Bracewell, Mitchell Santner (C), Nathan Smith, Matt Henry, Will O'Rourke.

Zimbabwe (Playing XI) - Brian Bennett, Ben Curran, Nick Welch, Sean Williams, Craig Ervine (C), Sikandar Raza, Tafadzwa Tsiga (WK), Newman Nyamhuri, Vincent Masekesa, Blessing Muzarabani, Tanaka Chivanga.
TOSS - Zimbabwe have won the toss and elected to BAT first.

New Zealand, led by Mitchell Santner in the absence of injured captain Tom Latham, will start the series as clear favorites with a balanced and experienced squad. Despite suffering an injury setback with Glenn Phillips ruled out, they've added Michael Bracewell to the team, although he'll leave after the first Test to play in The Hundred. Matthew Fisher is close to making his Test debut, and the pace attack will consist of Will O'Rourke, Matt Henry, and Jacob Duffy. With a strong team, the visitors will aim to continue their winning streak against Zimbabwe, using this series as an opportunity to get back into the rhythm of red-ball cricket. Stay tuned for toss and team updates.

Zimbabwe are looking to end their losing streak against New Zealand in the Test format. With a refreshed squad that includes Sikandar Raza, Roy Kaia, and Tanunurwa Makoni, the hosts will be eager to put up a strong fight. Blessing Muzarabani will lead the pace attack, and Trevor Gwandu will look to trouble the Kiwi batters. There's also speculation about a potential return for Brendan Taylor after serving his ban for spot-fixing, although he's not part of the squad yet. Surprisingly, Richard Ngarava has been overlooked for this Test series.

The stage is set for an exciting two-match Test series between Zimbabwe and New Zealand, with the first match starting today at the Queens Sports Club in Bulawayo. This series promises to be a thrilling encounter.
